text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert — ECC correctable error surge detected on inference-pool-usw2. Metrics: corrected_ecc > 8x baseline across 6 hosts. Multiple kernel Xid entries observed and several containers auto-restarted by kubelet. Pager: @ashley (oncall)

ashley (oncall): on it. quick snapshot — which hosts? any pattern (same rack/HW)?

devon: seeing it on gpu-nf-12, gpu-nf-13, gpu-nf-14, gpu-nf-21, gpu-nf-22, gpu-nf-23. rack A3 mostly. kernel logs show repeated Xid 13/31 entries plus nv-host-reset traces.

maddie: thanks. can we reduce batch sizes or temporarily throttle long-running jobs to reduce mem pressure while we triage?

ashley (oncall): yes. rolling throttle policy: 50% batch_size for jobs tagged `high-throughput` in inference namespace. applying now.

devon: nvidia-smi dump from gpu-nf-12 (appears noisy):
```
$ nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,DRIVER,UTILIZATION
==============NVSMI LOG==============
GPU 0
    ECC errors
      Volatile
        single bit:  128
        double bit:  0
    Driver Model: N/A
    Xid errors: Xid 13, Xid 31 logged in last 5m
    Utilization: 95 %
```

maddie: that single-bit ECC climb looks suspicious. maybe HW flapping under load. i'll start cordon+drain prep for the 3 worst hosts (nf-12/13/14). want to keep at least 2 spare nodes in pool.

ashley (oncall): go for cordon on nf-12/13/14. use `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` and move live sessions to fallback model variants. commands below:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-nf-12
kubectl drain gpu-nf-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl cordon gpu-nf-13
kubectl drain gpu-nf-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

infra-bot: Autoscaling paused for cluster inference-pool-usw2 by policy during incident. No new nodes will be provisioned automatically.

sean: customer impact? latency or error spike reported?

customer-bridge: customer telemetry showing spikes in 95p latency and a 1.8% increase in `model_error` for customers `acme-corp` and `brightline`. Health checks show transient 503s for a subset of requests routed to the affected nodes. Bridge created: zoom link in #customer-bridge if we need to spin up a bridge.

devon: digging kernel logs from gpu-nf-12 — paste tail of dmesg: 
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (0001:13): Ch 00000000, PID 2345, 00000000 00000000
[ 12345.679010] NVRM: Rm init failed, attempting recovery
[ 12345.679120] nvidia-nvlink: nvlink_tdr_handler: nvlink down
[ 12345.679230] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```

ashley (oncall): that 'fallen off the bus' message suggests either thermal/hardware or driver glitch. I've requested immediate hardware telepresence for rack A3 — ticket created: INFRA-1452.

maddie: meanwhile, to reduce blast radius, i'll add a temporary routing rule to avoid scheduling new heavy infer jobs to nodes in rack A3 and enable fast-fallback to CPU-backed replicas for specific customers. patching route table now.

ashley (oncall): applied throttle and route patch. Confirming no new pods scheduled on cordoned hosts and batch jobs reduced.

devon: for safe data collection before rebooting, please capture persistent logs and run `nvidia-bug-report.sh` on nf-12/13/14. attaching command: 
```
sudo /usr/bin/nvidia-bug-report.sh --output-file /tmp/nvidia-bug-nf12.tar.gz
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-drm
```

infra-bot: Note — automatic kernel livepatch disabled on the hosts due to conflicting NV drivers; manual patching required if driver roll needed.

sean: prioritize customers — are acme and brightline low-latency SLAs? do we need a customer-facing notice?

customer-bridge: acme has a P2 SLA, brightline is P3. acme already on bridge. Recommend short maintenance note with ETA 2 hours unless hardware team reports longer.

ashley (oncall): setting incident severity to sev2 for now and opening an incident channel. Escalating to HW crew for rack-level check and to SRE to validate driver compatibility matrix. I'll hand off to devon for night run. devon — you're taking next shift?

devon: taking handoff. my checklist: capture bug report, cordon/drain done, throttle enforced, customer bridge created, INFRA-1452 assigned, patch routing in place. I'll kick off a rolling reboot of the 3 hosts if hardware team gives go.

maddie: quick note — if we see Xid 62 tomorrow flip to persistent, we'll plan for a full hot-swap of GPUs on affected hosts. For now, avoid rolling restarts of other racks.

ashley (oncall): thanks team. I'll add a postmortem placeholder and assign owners for follow-up: devon (triage & logs), maddie (routing/throttle), infra (hardware diagnostics). Please add any additional notes to INFRA-1452. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident channel created: #incident-5101234567-ecc-sparkline — automated pings enabled.

customer-bridge: acme on call acknowledges maintenance; will notify downstream eng leads.

devon: handing off to oncall-next. last check: overall cluster latency down ~12% but error spike contained to affected hosts. will monitor and update every 30m.

ashley (oncall): thanks — oncall rotation will pick up. follow-up action: collect `nvidia-bug-report` artifacts and attach to INFRA-1452, and schedule postmortem if root cause is hardware.

maddie: copying suggested `kubectl` commands and the bug-report path into the ticket. signing off for now. :white_check_mark:
